stem: What is the safety purpose of an anti-free-flow mechanism in an IV infusion administration set?

options.A: Prevent uncontrolled gravity flow of IV fluid or medication when the set is not being controlled by the pump.
options.B: Increase the programmed infusion rate when an occlusion occurs.
options.C: Eliminate the need to monitor the infusion and patient.
options.D: Convert an IV administration set into an enteral feeding set.

rationale: FDA device safety information identifies uncontrolled flow and over-infusion as serious infusion-pump hazards. FDA recall information involving anti-free-flow components demonstrates that failure to clamp tubing after removal from a pump can permit free flow and cause dangerous medication over-infusion. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Explain how anti-free-flow mechanisms reduce uncontrolled IV infusion and overdose risk.

correction_summary: Removed conversational padding and reframed the item around the precise function of anti-free-flow protection. FDA device-safety and recall evidence directly support the uncontrolled-flow hazard. Difficulty reduced from hard to easy.
audit_findings: FDA sources support uncontrolled-flow/over-infusion risk and the anti-free-flow mechanism. A is uniquely correct; B-D are unrelated or unsafe. Independent second pass passed.
